subject: LLM API cutover discovery & next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: LLM API cutover discovery & next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier, Alice — good to meet. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key pain points you called out
- Monthly spend on proprietary APIs (OpenAI + Anthropic) has increased unpredictably as endpoints scaled.
- Latency spikes for production scoring traffic during peak hours impacting UX.
- Platform lock-in concerns: custom function-calling and streaming implementations tied to vendor SDKs.
- Auditing and longer retention requirements (12+ months) for inference logs.

Current stack (as described on call)
- Models: OpenAI gpt-4.1 for chat, Anthropic Claude-2 for assistant flows (hybrid).
- Infra: hosted SaaS for model calls; most orchestration in Kubernetes with a small in-house gateway.
- Integrations: user-facing chat + batch scoring pipelines; webhooks to downstream analytics.

Success criteria for a migration project
- 30–40% predictable reduction in per-token cost or equivalent unit economics.
- No regressions on key prompts (<=4% quality delta on your eval set).
- Production latency at or below current 95th percentile SLA (200ms target for scoring flows).
- Security/compliance: SOC2-equivalent controls, ability to retain/purge logs by policy.

Compatibility constraints you flagged
- Must support streaming token-level responses and function/tool-calling semantics.
- Need to preserve existing prompt engineering wrappers and metadata headers.
- Require signed BAA and encryption of logs at-rest.

Proposed next steps
1) You: share a short list of 6–10 representative prompts/evals and current P95 latency numbers for the scoring flows (Alice, you mentioned you could share a pared-down eval set).
2) Us: Redwood to produce a short compatibility checklist + model shortlist (quantized variants included) and a preliminary cost delta estimate (we'll surface the assumptions).
3) Security: exchange security questionnaire and schedule a call with our security lead (Vivek) for SOC2, KMS and log-retention details.
4) Tech deep-dive: propose a 60-minute technical session next week to walk infra, integration, and a small smoke-test plan.

Attachments: we can share an early cost sketch — I'll attach initial_mae_estimates.xlsx in the forward to our team.

If this aligns, I'll loop in Monica to prepare the compatibility checklist and Vivek for the security items. Preferred tech deep-dive slots: Tue 2026-07-07 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 2026-07-08 09:00–10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Alice Park <alice@nebulahealth.com>

Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LLM API cutover discovery & next steps

Thanks, Rishi — this is a helpful recap and matches our notes. A few clarifications and some items from our side: 

1) Volume & spend
- We do ~2.6M input tokens / month for scoring + ~12M tokens for chat. Current combined monthly invoice is averaging $45k. We want a predictable pricing model or predictable delta vs today.

2) Compatibility priorities
- Streaming and token-level access are mandatory for the chat product.
- Function/tool calling: we use a JSON-schema-based tool-calling layer; any replacement must expose the same call/response hooks or we accept a small adapter implementation.

3) Security/regulatory
- Required: SOC2 Type II, BAA, per-tenant KMS support, and RBAC for access to logs.
- We'll need evidence for data deletion policies and a sample audit log schema.

4) Success metrics: agree with your list. For quality, we'll provide a 150-prompt eval set — mostly clinical triage and FAQ style prompts.

I'll upload the eval set and redacted latency numbers to the Drive link by EOD tomorrow. Attaching our security questionnaire (Nebula_Security_Q3.pdf).

On timing: Tue Jul 7 10:00 PT works for me. Please invite anyone who will own the migration plan and a security/data-retention engineer.

Best,
Alice Park
Head of ML Ops, Nebula Health
alice@nebulahealth.com

Folks — forwarding the reply from Alice at Nebula. Short asks from me before the tech deep-dive on Tue: 

Action items
- Monica: can you draft the compatibility checklist (streaming, function-calling shim, headers, eval harness) and a shortlist of 3 candidate open models (quantized variants where applicable) with rough token-cost deltas vs Nebula's $45k/mo baseline? Please include suggested rollback/fallback options.
- Vivek: Alice flagged SOC2, BAA, KMS per-tenant and audit log samples. Can you prepare our SOC2 evidence bundle + a short one-pager on how our private deployment supports per-tenant KMS and log retention / deletion flows?
- Tessa: help coordinate calendar invite for Tue Jul 7 10:00 PT; invitees from our side: Rishi (solutions), Monica (technical owner), Vivek (security), and an infra engineer (we can add Mateo or Lukas). From Nebula: Alice + 1 infra person + legal (optional).

I'm attaching the initial cost sketch I referenced for context. This is intentionally high level; we'll refine after we get their eval set and our model-run benchmarks.

Thanks — will align on a dry-run for the demo on Mon afternoon if needed.

Rishi

Thanks — I'm on it. Quick notes before the Tue deep-dive (we should have slides for each):

Compatibility checklist (high level)
- Streaming: verify token-level delta and client keep-alive semantics.
- Tool-calling shim: map Nebula's JSON-schema -> our function-calling adapter (estimate: few hundred lines, <1 sprint to prototype).
- Prompt wrappers: preserve metadata headers for attribution & telemetry.
- Eval harness: run Nebula's 150-prompt set against candidate models + current vendor baselines.

Model shortlist (prelim)
- Llama-3-Chat (8B quantized variant) — strong latency/cost balance for scoring.
- Mistral-Instruct-16B (quantized) — better hallucination profile on instruction prompts.
- Redstone-7B (private-vpc optimized) — lower memory footprint for private deployments (note: still in verification).

Security & compliance
- Vivek: please bring the SOC2 evidence and a onepager on per-tenant KMS. Alice requested audit log schema — I recommend we prepare a short sample log file that shows fields they care about (request_id, user_id, model_version, input_hash, token_count, timestamp).

Operational asks for the deep-dive
- Nebula to provide: eval set (150 prompts), redacted P95 numbers, and an example of their tool-calling JSON schema.
- Redwood to provide: compatibility checklist, 2-week smoke-test plan, cost delta slides, and a short demo plan to show streaming + function-calling parity.

I'll draft the slides and circulate before EOD Monday for review. Tue 10:00 PT invite pending.

Monica Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai
